55

64	and nothing decides between them. Otherwise write for the most likely reader and name that

68	
69	Ask what the reader is doing when they open the page.
70	
71	| The reader is | Job | It holds | It leaves out |
72	|---|---|---|---|
73	| learning by doing | Tutorial | one path that works, a visible result at every step | options, alternatives, explanation beyond a clause |
74	| working toward a goal | How-to guide | the steps to that goal, for a competent reader | teaching, background, the full list of options |
75	| looking up a fact mid-task | Reference | description only, complete, in the shape of the thing described | instructions, opinion, history |

79	mixed page: a short piece of each job, with links to the rest. Before writing any of
80	these, or a runbook, release notes, a changelog entry, a pull request description, or a
81	commit message, read the entry for that document in `references/documents.md`.

84	
85	Read the source before drafting: the code paths the document describes, the build and
86	task files, the configuration, the existing docs. For each action the document will
87	mention, find its actor now. Run a command to confirm it only when the run changes
88	nothing (a read, `--help`, a dry run). Keep a list of what you could not confirm.

91	for, who is on call, which environment the steps target), ask before writing: two to four
92	questions, batched, in the conversation language. Do not ask what you can read yourself.
93	When the user wants the document before they can answer, write it and mark each hole
94	where it falls, as a `TODO` that says what is missing. Never paper over a hole, and list
95	every one in the reply.

98	
99	Draft with the rules of the next section. Then go through the draft one verb at a time
100	and ask "who or what does this?" The sentence has to answer.
101	
102	Rebecca Johnson's test finds the passives fast: if "by zombies" fits after the verb, the
103	verb is passive ("por zumbis" in Portuguese). "The cache is invalidated [by zombies] on

105	missing name is what you now look up. The test catches only the first of the six places

107	
108	- **A passive without its agent.** "The cache is invalidated on deploy" becomes "The
109	  deploy job invalidates the cache".
110	- **A noun that swallowed the verb.** "After validation of the token" becomes "After the
111	  gateway validates the token".
112	- **A subject that means nothing.** "It is recommended to", "there is a retry", "é
113	  necessário configurar". Write who recommends, what retries, who configures.
114	- **A catch-all actor.** "The system", "the application", "the process", when the system
115	  has several parts. Name the part.
116	- **An instruction written as a description.** "The variable must be set" becomes "Set
117	  the variable". The actor is the reader, so use the imperative.
118	- **In Portuguese, the forms with "se".** "Envia-se", "configura-se", "deve-se" hide the
119	  actor as "é enviado" does.

122

124	  audit log does not record by whom."

126	  written in Go." "This endpoint is deprecated."

129	follows one thing through the system and that thing should stay at the front of the
130	sentence, give it an active verb: "The request then goes to the gateway, which signs it".

133	Portuguese. Read it when a sentence resists the rewrite, when the document is in
134	Portuguese, or when you review a text you did not write.

145	- The first paragraph alone tells the reader what this is and whether to read on.
146	- The document does one job. Material for another job is a link.
147	- Each thing has one name, and it is the name the code uses.
148	- A final read as the reader fixed in step 1, from the top, doing what the page says.

151	
152	### The document
153	
154	- Lead with the point. The first paragraph says what the thing is and what the reader
155	  gets from the page, in words they would search for. Many readers stop there.
156	- State what the document covers, and what it leaves out that a reader would expect to
157	  find. Put prerequisites before the first step.
158	- A heading says what its section holds. A heading for a task starts with a verb.
159	- Cut what the reader's task does not need. Link to a detail instead of repeating it.
160

162	
163	- The first sentence states the point of the paragraph. One topic per paragraph.
164	- Start a sentence with what the reader already has, and end it with what is new. The
165	  end of the sentence is where the reader puts the emphasis.

167	  compared on the same attributes, and prose for reasoning, because a list drops the
168	  connectives. Introduce a list with a full sentence and keep its items parallel.
169

171	
172	- Actor, verb, object, in that order, with the subject next to its verb.
173	- Let the verb carry the action: "validates", not "performs the validation of".
174	- One idea per sentence. Put the condition before the instruction: "To roll back, run…",
175	  "If the check fails, restart the worker".
176	- Present tense. Address the reader as "you", in the form of address the house uses.
177	- Prefer the positive form, and never stack negatives: "the job retries once the lock
178	  is free", not "the job does not retry unless the lock is not held".

180	  acted on, and "p95 above 800 ms" and "`ERR_QUOTA`" can.

183

185	  second thing.

187	  document uses it several times.

189	  the noun.

191	- Leave "simply", "just", "easy", and "obviously" out of instructions. They tell the
192	  reader who is stuck that the fault is theirs.

195

197	  before what: "In `config/app.yaml`, set…".

201	  placeholder as `<name>` and say what replaces it.

203	  what it prints.

208	every fact (contract 4), and change what the rules above call for. A passive whose actor

213	or a fact that only they know, a reader the document never settles) and proposed edits,

227	  changed.
228	- **A short text** (a pull request description, a commit message). Reply with the text
229	  ready to paste. Do not post or commit it unless the user asked.
230

232	open, and the commands you did not run. Do not summarize the document.
233

235	
236	| File | Read it when |
237	|---|---|
238	| `references/documents.md` | Before writing or reviewing a specific kind of document: what each one must hold, its order, and its usual failure. |
239	| `references/actors.md` | A sentence resists the actor pass, the document is in Portuguese, or you review a text you did not write. |

242

248	Guide, the US federal plain language guidelines, Write the Docs, and George Gopen and

# Export pipeline

This page describes what happens to an export request.

## Request

When an export is requested, the payload is validated. Requests above 100,000 rows are
rejected. If the payload is valid, a job is enqueued and a `202` is returned.

## Processing

The job is picked up and the CSV file is generated. The file is encrypted before it is
uploaded to the bucket. If something goes wrong, the job is retried up to three times,
after which it is moved to the dead-letter queue.

## Delivery

Once the upload is done, a download link is sent by email. The link is expired after
24 hours.

## Backups

Backups of the bucket are rotated weekly.

    if payload.get("rows", 0) > MAX_ROWS:
        raise HTTPException(413, f"exports above {MAX_ROWS} rows are not supported")


@app.post("/exports", status_code=202)

    validate_payload(payload)
    connection = pika.BlockingConnection(pika.URLParameters(os.environ["QUEUE_URL"]))
    channel = connection.channel()
    channel.basic_publish(exchange="", routing_key="exports", body=json.dumps(payload))
    connection.close()

import os

LINK_TTL_SECONDS = 24 * 60 * 60


def notify(account_id: str, key: str) -> None:
    url = boto3.client("s3").generate_presigned_url(
        "get_object",
        Params={"Bucket": os.environ["EXPORT_BUCKET"], "Key": key},
        ExpiresIn=LINK_TTL_SECONDS,
    )
    boto3.client("ses").send_email(
        Source=os.environ["MAIL_FROM"],
        Destination={"ToAddresses": [f"{account_id}@accounts.example.com"]},
        Message={

import json
import os

import boto3
import pika
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

from exporter.notifier import notify

MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3


def build_csv(job: dict) -> bytes:
    rows = [f"{job['account_id']},{n}" for n in range(job.get("rows", 0))]
    return "\n".join(rows).encode()


def handle(channel, method, properties, body) -> None:
    job = json.loads(body)
    attempts = (properties.headers or {}).get("x-attempts", 0) + 1
    try:
        data = Fernet(os.environ["EXPORT_KEY"]).encrypt(build_csv(job))
        key = f"{job['account_id']}/{method.delivery_tag}.csv.enc"
        boto3.client("s3").put_object(Bucket=os.environ["EXPORT_BUCKET"], Key=key, Body=data)
        notify(job["account_id"], key)
    except Exception:
        target = "exports.dead" if attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS else "exports"
        channel.basic_publish(
            exchange="",
            routing_key=target,
            body=body,
            properties=pika.BasicProperties(headers={"x-attempts": attempts}),
        )
    channel.basic_ack(method.delivery_tag)


def main() -> None:
    connection = pika.BlockingConnection(pika.URLParameters(os.environ["QUEUE_URL"]))
    channel = connection.channel()
    channel.basic_consume(queue="exports", on_message_callback=handle)
    channel.start_consuming()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Export pipeline

This page describes what happens to an export request.

## Request

When an export is requested, the payload is validated. Requests above 100,000 rows are
rejected. If the payload is valid, a job is enqueued and a `202` is returned.

## Processing

The job is picked up and the CSV file is generated. The file is encrypted before it is
uploaded to the bucket. If something goes wrong, the job is retried up to three times,
after which it is moved to the dead-letter queue.

## Delivery

Once the upload is done, a download link is sent by email. The link is expired after
24 hours.

## Backups

Backups of the bucket are rotated weekly.

**Dois pontos do código que o runbook trata de forma explícita:**
- O worker captura qualquer exceção e não registra o erro em log nem na mensagem. Por isso o passo "descubra a causa" lista só as dependências que o código chama (`EXPORT_KEY`, `EXPORT_BUCKET`, `MAIL_FROM`, `QUEUE_URL`). Ele deixa claro que essa lista mostra onde a falha pode nascer, e não a causa atual. A última seção sugere registrar a exceção em `exporter/worker.py`.
- `requeue_dead.py` publica a mensagem sem o contador `x-attempts`. Cada mensagem recolocada ganha três tentativas novas, e o runbook avisa isso antes do passo. Por isso ele manda corrigir a causa antes de recolocar e começar com `--limit 5`.

**Leitor assumido:** o engenheiro de plantão, possivelmente novo no serviço.

**Comandos:** não rodei nenhum. O script precisa de um RabbitMQ real. Copiei as flags `--dry-run` e `--limit` do código do script. Não usei o `unslop`, porque não está instalado nesta sessão.
